reasoning: By Turán's theorem, a triangle-free graph on 13 vertices has at most the edges of the balanced complete bipartite graph. Splitting the vertices into parts of sizes 6 and 7 and joining every vertex across the parts gives K₆,₇, which has 6·7 = 42 edges and contains no triangle. Thus the maximum is 42.
